# Slice 4 evidence fixtures

The fixture creates a disposable backend/none host with an explicitly selected product package. It never fills in this repository's unconfigured host fields. The public sample covers accepted decisions, requirements, traced acceptance criteria, contracts and derived usage, including a combined-document variant.

- Package fixtures exercise closed schema and metadata, unsafe Windows/POSIX syntax, traversal, symlinks, hardlinks, case collisions, dependencies, reading order, responsibility ownership, stable anchors, scope, traceability and exact-byte integrity.
- Task fixtures exercise fresh package provenance, the private active chunk, typed references, applicability declarations and exact source extracts (only CRLF/LF transport normalization).
- Definition fixtures exercise unresolved material questions, independent-review receipt consistency, explicit matching approval after review, amended versions, stale candidates, safe write/rename failures and concurrent changes. Fixture reviewer/human strings are synthetic test data; they do not demonstrate live independent review or actual human identity.
- HUD fixtures exercise draft, awaiting approval, approved, invalidated, missing input, stale review, spoofed readiness and temporary mid-write states. Polling renders fresh evidence without modifying files.
- Workflow checks verify instruction adoption and an obedient caller's gate. They do not prove physical agent/IDE interception. The existing Slice 3 installed Git hook is a separate mechanism.
- Public/private separation is tested by deleting private orchestration and reading public product links. Semantic document completeness and genuine approval remain human-supervised.

Run `pnpm test:tophat` on Node 24 or later. Existing Slice 1–3 regressions remain included. No fixture invokes Git mutation, Linear, package installation, a model, or a live IDE hook.
